surfaces.name: ralph-qa
surfaces.reason: independent verify loop (ralplan+critic logic): a backbone of 3+ reviewer agents on the session model always runs (Claude=Plan without a model, Codex=spawn_agent without a role or forked context; read-only by instruction); --codex/--gemini/--opencode seat that CLI's best model (asks when ambiguous, configured default when nobody can be asked), a node runner (references/seat-run.mjs) makes the private folders and the payload (a diff that carries the listed new files, made through a copy of the index), scans it, sends each seat from its own copy with answers kept elsewhere under a 600 s limit that ends the seat's whole process group, and cleans up (codex read-only with its shell tool, exec-policy rules, MCP servers, sub-agents, hooks, notify, web search, metrics and OpenTelemetry off, not seated when a managed config or a requirements file overrides those; gemini under a deny-all admin policy that a helper checks first, with no MCP servers, extensions or prompt telemetry, its error reports kept in the answer folder, and its session records removed after, those of runs cut short too; opencode as a per-run deny-all agent reading the payload on stdin, auto-compaction off). Seat-lifecycle monotone gate (INCONCLUSIVE on seat loss); runtime-aware

surfaces.name: smart-compact
surfaces.reason: context-threshold compaction-hygiene gate (statusLine detect + hook bridge + assistant chain + TUI handoff); runtime-aware
surfaces.caveat: Claude Code detects through a statusLine wrapper; Codex through scripts/codex-gate.mjs: on copies it to $CODEX_HOME/hooks-custom/banker-smart-compact-gate.mjs (out of any workspace, since Codex runs trusted hooks outside the sandbox) and appends a UserPromptSubmit group for it last in hooks.json (PowerShell call form on Windows); the hook reads the rollout's last token_count (last_token_usage over model_context_window). Codex runs it only after the user trusts it (Hooks need review, /hooks); on/off write ~/.codex, so under workspace-write they need approval to run outside the sandbox (not --add-dir ~/.codex); run off before removing banker or OMX

surfaces.name: visual-ralph

surfaces.reason: opt-in, typed by the person only (disable-model-invocation; Codex agents/openai.yaml allow_implicit_invocation: false): sets Claude Code permissions.defaultMode to bypassPermissions after a risk warning and an explicit confirmation; node script first, python3/PowerShell fallback when node cannot run, a command the person runs when the account may not write; off restores; Codex leaves its own approval policy alone

surfaces.name: setup-sandbox
surfaces.reason: agent sandbox per-OS (bubblewrap+userns / AppContainer / Seatbelt) + rust/cargo + git safe.directory; Codex sandbox_mode

surfaces.name: setup-harness-factory
surfaces.reason: installs+configures+guides the revfactory/harness team-architecture factory plugin (Claude harness@harness-marketplace, Codex SaehwanPark/meta-harness); Apache-2.0 referenced not redistributed

surfaces.name: obsidizer
surfaces.reason: AI-wiki -> Obsidian graph normalize/interlink; LLM semantic edits + zero-input deterministic canonicalizer, runtime-agnostic; in-place durable
surfaces.caveat: OMC-managed trees: 9-field frontmatter envelope + reserved files + no-rename + bare [[slug]] links only (extractWikiLinks slugifies piped/heading forms -> broken-ref); aliases written in generic vaults only; Canvas sidecars and body-inline :: are durable in-place; uses wiki_lint read-only. --enable is Claude-only (Codex has no MCP tool hooks) and is an honest no-op on Codex.

surfaces.name: ultra-interview
surfaces.reason: research-first interview that resolves what public sources can answer and asks the human only what they alone can decide; discrete checklist gate (unresolved/total) instead of a scalar self-score
surfaces.caveat: does NOT bundle or replace the OMC/OMX native deep-interview. Owns its own rubric on purpose: OMC scores 3 dimensions and OMX scores 5, so inheriting a native score would make the same threshold mean different things per runtime. Regulatory lookup is a general 'find the jurisdiction's primary source' instruction, not a hardcoded endpoint.

surfaces.name: interval-report
surfaces.reason: human-facing progress ledger at docs/intermission.md for long runs; thin time layer + renderer over whatever state exists
surfaces.caveat: start time is persisted in the file and never re-stamped (a compaction/resume re-stamp collapses elapsed to 0 and biases the report optimistic exactly when it matters most). Wall-clock comes from `date` because neither runtime exposes hour:minute in context. Reads ultragoal state when present but never duplicates it; leaves compaction triggering to smart-compact.

surfaces.name: summary-wiki
surfaces.reason: read-only digest of the wiki into a single docs/ file for a knowledge-sync review (what the user knows vs what the wiki accumulated)
surfaces.caveat: Claude = wiki_* MCP over .omc/wiki; Codex = `omx wiki` CLI over omx_wiki/ (there is NO wiki_* MCP on Codex; do not copy the append_wiki/compact-wiki caveat wording). Enumerates .omc/wiki/*.md directly and never wiki_list, which reads a structurally stale index and silently omits pages. Read-only toward the wiki; distinct from compact-wiki, which mutates it in place.

surfaces.name: update-banker
surfaces.reason: updates an installed banker across its three independently-drifting channels (Claude plugin / npm global CLI / Codex skills)
surfaces.caveat: the axis is channel, not OS: banker has zero dependencies and copy-based install, so OS differences reduce to npm prefix/EACCES footnotes. npm must be updated FIRST and verified before `banker setup --codex`, because setup sweeps every banker-* before copying and a stale CLI restores only its own older manifest. Verdicts come from per-channel probes, never exit codes.

surfaces.name: refresh-readme
surfaces.reason: brings a README back in line with the code it drifted from, before release; prose claims are cross-checked against the manifest, skills/, and package.json
surfaces.caveat: README only. Fence/inline-code/URL/--flag aware: POSIX end-of-options ` -- ` is textually identical to prose double-hyphen, so a blanket sed/awk substitution is itself a defect. Delegates AI-writing markers to humanizer rather than restating them.

surfaces.name: cleansing-memory
surfaces.reason: keeps agent memory files inside their documented thresholds by de-duping to latest, condensing losslessly, and converting append-style records into replace-style
surfaces.caveat: only MEMORY.md has a documented hard gate (200 lines or 25KB, whichever comes first); CLAUDE.md has NO documented size limit, so asserting a byte cap for it would be fabrication. Codex's 32768-byte project_doc_max_bytes covers project-scope AGENTS.md only, not the global one, and truncates raw bytes before a lossy UTF-8 decode, so cutting to an exact byte count corrupts the boundary character. Codebase-derivable CLAUDE.md trimming is left to Claude's own /doctor.

surfaces.name: motion-graphic-setup

surfaces.caveat: needs Node+ffmpeg; hyperframes npx-installed (Apache-2.0)

surfaces.name: motion-graphic-make
surfaces.reason: thin wrapper delegating to hyperframes /motion-graphics (free form categories); owns no render pipeline, only the stage gates (plan approval, snapshot and render review, independent check) and the review page and preview server it shares with 3d-intro-build; runtime-agnostic
surfaces.caveat: needs hyperframes via motion-graphic-setup (npx, Apache-2.0); the three references are byte-identical copies of 3d-intro-build's (scripts/sync-adapter.js)

surfaces.name: 3d-intro-setup
surfaces.reason: collects Azure creds (direct or console-sample parse) to untracked env + FREE preflight; installs Node/ffmpeg; runtime-agnostic

surfaces.name: 3d-intro-build
surfaces.reason: scroll-scrub 3D intro: gpt-image stills, WAN key pool video with Sora-2 fallback (forward-chaining, or the optional hold-and-flight mode), a review page for every paid stage, a page with no inline script or style (strict CSP), optional scene-by-scene navigation and glass panel, and a Playwright measurement for the independent check; vendored scroll-world engine (MIT) left unmodified; cross-platform Node
surfaces.caveat: the independent check (verify-intro.mjs) needs Node Playwright with Chromium (setup-playwright); the hold-and-flight mode needs WAN keys and is not yet confirmed by a paid smoke

surfaces.name: payload-mon
surfaces.reason: toggles an estimated API request payload segment (bytes against Claude Code's 32MB request limit) in the OMC custom HUD statusline, beside ctx; pure Node, no deps
surfaces.caveat: measures Claude Code sessions only (the 32MB limit and the transcript format are Claude Code's); run from Codex it still manages the same machine's Claude Code HUD wrapper but never measures Codex's own requests. Under Codex's workspace-write sandbox, on and off need approval to run outside it (not --add-dir ~/.claude, which would let the session rewrite hooks); status only reads. Needs the OMC custom HUD wrapper (setup-omc-hud); the wrapper imports a module copy kept beside it because plugin install paths are versioned and retired on update

surfaces.name: tone-compact
surfaces.reason: turns compact Korean writing rules (ASD-STE100 based: lists and tables, transliterated terms, no decorative symbols) on or off across sessions; pure Node, no deps
surfaces.caveat: per runtime: Claude Code gets <config>/rules/banker-tone-compact.md; Codex gets one marked block at the end of $CODEX_HOME/AGENTS.override.md (when it has content of its own) or AGENTS.md, wrapped in USER:OMX:POLICY so omx setup --merge-agents and a plain omx setup with team mode on keep it (--force, a confirmed overwrite or a plain omx setup with team mode off replace the file; run on again). Turning it on in one runtime leaves the other as it is

surfaces.name: omc-patch
surfaces.reason: re-applies local OMC hook patches after an OMC auto-update and pins the OMC marketplace origin; finds a timeout helper an older kit left inside a block (hooks such as project-memory silently off) and fixes it by reverting the active folder and patching again; probes the project-memory hook in a scratch project; pure Node, no deps
surfaces.caveat: acts on the Claude Code OMC plugin cache under ~/.claude even when run from Codex; under Codex's workspace-write sandbox --check and probe-pm run as they are, while apply and revert need approval to run outside it (not --add-dir ~/.claude); TARGET_VERSION 5.7.0 is hard-coded in the tool and only a plain apply uses it; the skill passes --no-update on every apply and check; --root touches one plugin folder only and never the marketplace pin

surfaces.name: remains
surfaces.reason: finds remaining bugs, defects and unverified items and shows them in one table; runs the project's tests on registered SSH test boxes; pure Node, no deps
surfaces.caveat: box runs need ssh, scp and git on this machine and key-only SSH logins; boxes are registered in ~/.config/banker/test-boxes.json; read and test only, never fixes or pushes

surfaces.name: trouble-shooting
surfaces.reason: investigates a problem and reports symptom, problem, cause, fix and action plan in one table, one row per problem; --no-plan stops at the fix; report only, never fixes

surfaces.name: ultra-chain
surfaces.reason: orchestrates nine stages in order: deep-research, ultra-interview, ralplan --deliberate followed by a ralph-qa plan quorum of 3+ reviewers (ralplan has two reviewers and no way to add more), a mock the user approves, ralph --critic=critic (Codex: OMX ralph plus a critic loop, since OMX ralph has no --critic), tests on the registered OS boxes fed to a ralph-qa quorum, visual review (machine diff against the mock, screenshots, an independent verdict), a process report rendered from its own ledger, and local sharing; Claude=OMC 5, Codex=OMX; body runtime-aware; pure Node helpers, no deps
surfaces.caveat: uses the sibling banker skills deep-research, ultra-interview, ralph-qa and remains (boxes.mjs); box runs need ssh, scp and git with key-only logins in ~/.config/banker/test-boxes.json; screenshots need Playwright with Chromium; serve.mjs and preview-lib.mjs are byte-identical copies of 3d-intro-build's (scripts/sync-adapter.js); never pushes, opens a PR or posts outside without an explicit request

surfaces.name: anti-drm
surfaces.reason: turns on or off rules that steer the agent away from the file extensions a network-separated PC's DRM encrypts (default .txt .pdf .ppt .pptx .doc .docx .hwp .hwpx .xls .xlsx .csv) toward replacements (.md .html .tsv); asks the extensions on first use and keeps them in ~/.config/banker/anti-drm.json; pure Node, no deps
surfaces.caveat: the same places as tone-compact (shared module instruction-toggle.mjs): Claude Code gets <config>/rules/banker-anti-drm.md; Codex gets one marked block wrapped in USER:OMX:POLICY at the end of AGENTS.md, or AGENTS.override.md when it has content of its own. The settings are shared by both runtimes; on and off act on one runtime, while config and on with settings refresh every runtime that holds the rules. It never decrypts or converts files DRM already protects; it only picks the extensions of files the agent newly creates. The organization's security rules come first

surfaces.name: theme-selection
surfaces.reason: applies 74 themes to a project as CSS custom properties, light and dark (148 combinations), with contrast correction; also emits a theme picker (markup and two scripts) and a contrast audit (check), and reads the project's DESIGN.md as more themes; pure Node, no deps, no network
surfaces.caveat: the bundled palettes derive from VoltAgent/awesome-design-md (MIT; LICENSE and NOTICE.md in assets/); theme names only point at the sites the designs reference, and the trademarks belong to their owners; --out overwrites the file it names (refused when that file itself is a symbolic link), so the skill asks first when that file exists

surfaces.name: front-qa
surfaces.reason: ralplan->ralph frontend-QA pipeline; Claude=OMC, Codex=OMX

surfaces.name: setup
surfaces.reason: installer orchestrator; Claude AskUserQuestion multi-select, Codex prompt-based selection

surfaces.name: graceful-pause
surfaces.reason: Codex counterpart of the Claude Code /graceful-pause mod: sent mid-turn, Codex holds it until the running tool call ends and puts it into the same turn, so the session stops after the current step
surfaces.caveat: source in codex/skills/graceful-pause (the Claude plugin keeps its immediate /graceful-pause mod); relies on Codex steering a message typed while a turn runs (Codex 0.144.5: delivered after the next tool call)
